notes.1: Candidates did well to correctly read the volumes of liquids in the three measuring cylinders. It was not a straightforward question as each cylinder had different intervals between graduations.
notes.2: Most candidates were able to identify the car with the greatest average speed.
notes.3: Candidates did well to correctly interpret the speed-time graph.
notes.6: Candidates had little difficulty in calculating the density of the metal.
notes.9: This question was challenging for some candidates. They needed to recognise that a wind powered generation of electric energy is dependent on the wind strength while batteries can continuously supply power. Stronger candidates were able to deduce the more efficient supply when given the output per 1000 W input.
notes.11: While most candidates selected the right answer, A , large numbers of candidates chose each of the other three options.
notes.13: Many candidates did not read this question carefully enough. The question stated the area of one foot of the man and that he was standing with two feet on the ground. Nevertheless, a majority of candidates found the pressure exerted when the man was standing on one foot.
notes.17: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly. Other candidates chose the substance with the greatest temperature rise as the one with the largest thermal capacity rather than the one which had the smallest temperature rise.
notes.18: This question was challenging for many candidates, with most thinking that the greatest temperature difference between the ends of the bar would be the copper bar. In practice, this would have the smallest temperature rise because the energy is passed along the bar, warming the far end. Consequently, the largest temperature difference will be the bar which conducts least energy, where the far end of the bar is at the lowest temperature.
notes.20: Only stronger candidates recalled that light travels as a transverse wave, and amongst these candidates, many did not know that the vibrations in a transverse wave are at right angles to the direction of travel of the disturbance.
notes.21: Many candidates confused amplitude with wavelength and answered this incorrectly.
notes.28: Only the strongest candidates answered this question correctly. All incorrect options were chosen fairly equally by other candidates.
notes.36: The three-dimensional nature of the simple motor effect and the a.c. generator make them conceptually difficult. Nevertheless, the logic of the changes in this question allowed stronger candidates to identify the correct response.
notes.37: The structure of the atomic nucleus was not well known, with many candidates unable to identify the correct statement.
notes.39: This question was not answered well by many candidates.
